```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(rrad)
old_options <- options(rrad.offline = TRUE)
work <- tempfile("rrad-vignette-")
dir.create(work)
```

`rrad` brings RAD's demultiplexing, barcode discovery, and read reformatting
engines into R. It is the RAD companion package used by SIRUP and does not
require a separate RAD executable. This guide creates a small synthetic data
set and runs entirely offline. Its sequences demonstrate API behavior, not a
real sequencing chemistry or a statistical benchmark.

## Pack and inspect reads

Each synthetic read has an eight-base adapter, a four-base cell barcode, an
eight-base poly-T segment, and a short cDNA sequence. Quality strings must have
exactly the same lengths as their sequences. Phred offsets are explicit; they
are never guessed from input.

```{r pack}
sequences <- c("ACGTACGTAACCTTTTTTTTGATTACA",
               "ACGTACGTTTGATTTTTTTTCAGTCA")
reads <- rad_pack_reads(
  seq_id = c("read-1", "read-2"),
  seq = sequences,
  qual = strrep("I", nchar(sequences))
)
rad_validate(reads, deep = TRUE)
rad_qmean(reads)
rad_materialize(reads)
```

The result is a `data.table` with class `rad_reads`. The `seq_id`, `seq`, and
`qual` columns hold handles to a shared native store. Length and quality
summaries are ordinary numeric columns computed during ingestion. Filter by
these summaries without decoding all sequences:

```{r filter}
selected <- reads[reads$mean_q >= 20, ]
as.character(selected$seq)
```

Subsets share the original store. After discarding many reads,
`selected <- rad_compact(selected)` can rebuild a smaller store; the original
store is released when no remaining object refers to it. Use `rad_materialize()`
when another package requires character columns. Keep packed core columns
unchanged; repack a modified materialized table with `as_rad_reads()`.

## Discover a whitelist and demultiplex

Write a FASTQ file and an explicit CSV layout in the temporary working
directory. The layout's `whitelist` column is empty because this example will
provide the discovered whitelist directly.

```{r input-files}
fastq <- file.path(work, "reads.fastq")
rad_write_fastq(reads, fastq)
layout <- file.path(work, "layout.csv")
writeLines(c(
  "Read Layout,,,,,",
  "id,seq,expected_length,type,class,whitelist",
  "anchor,ACGTACGT,,static,linker,",
  "barcode,,4,variable,barcode,",
  "poly_t,TTTTTTTT,,static,poly_t,",
  "read,,,variable,read,"
), layout)
```

`rad_scan_wl()` finds barcodes following an adapter and writes a selected
whitelist plus counts and annotations. For this tiny example, use
`selection = "above_floor"` so both observed barcodes are retained. The default
`"high_specificity"` selection applies RAD's statistical barcode caller and is
intended for data sets with enough observations to estimate a count distribution.

```{r scan}
scan <- rad_scan_wl(
  input = fastq,
  output_prefix = file.path(work, "cells"),
  adapter_seq = "ACGTACGT",
  barcode_length = 4L,
  max_error = 0,
  selection = "above_floor",
  threads = 1L
)
readLines(scan$artifacts$whitelist)
```

Pass the selected whitelist into demultiplexing. The zero minimum cDNA length
is only for the short synthetic reads; choose a scientifically appropriate
filter for real data.

```{r demux}
run <- rad_demux(
  layout = layout,
  fastq = fastq,
  out_dir = file.path(work, "demux"),
  custom_whitelist = scan$artifacts$whitelist,
  min_read_length = 0L,
  threads = 1L
)
run$status
run$stats[c("total_reads", "reads_demultiplexed", "records_serialized")]
```

The primary gzip FASTQ contains the extracted reads with RAD's SAM-style
barcode tags. The `artifacts` list gives exact paths; use those paths instead
of reconstructing output filenames. For a single discovery-and-demultiplexing
call, use `auto_whitelist = TRUE` instead of `custom_whitelist`.

## Export pRESTO FASTA for IgBLAST

`rad_reformat()` accepts a demultiplexing result directly. An explicit output
path keeps the demultiplexed input available. Without an explicit path, a
non-splitting header or coordinate rewrite replaces its input after a successful
temporary write; FASTA conversion always requires an explicit output path.

```{r reformat}
fasta <- rad_reformat(
  run,
  to_fasta = TRUE,
  header_format = "presto",
  output_fastq = file.path(work, "igblast-input.fasta")
)
readLines(fasta$artifacts$fasta)
```

pRESTO output uses `QNAME|BARCODE=...|UMI=...`, omitting annotations absent
from the input. `BARCODE` prefers a spatial `BC:Z:` tag and otherwise uses
`CB:Z:`. This toy layout has no UMI, so its output has no UMI annotation.
`header_format = "preserve"` retains the original tags, while `"collapsed"`
uses RAD's legacy positional header. To split output by cell barcode, use
`split_bc = TRUE` with `out_dir`; splitting is always keyed by `CB:Z:`.

## Process larger files in chunks

`rad_read_fastq()` reads a file into one packed store. For bounded-memory
processing, open a stream, process one chunk at a time, and close it even if
processing fails. Each returned chunk owns its own store.

```{r streaming}
count_high_quality <- function(path, chunk_size = 50000L) {
  stream <- rad_stream(path)
  on.exit(rad_stream_close(stream), add = TRUE)
  total <- 0
  repeat {
    chunk <- rad_stream_next(stream, n = chunk_size)
    if (is.null(chunk)) break
    total <- total + sum(chunk$mean_q >= 20, na.rm = TRUE)
  }
  total
}
count_high_quality(fastq, chunk_size = 1L)
```

Use `rad_rbind_reads()` to combine independently owned chunks. Directly binding
their handle columns can associate handles with the wrong store. Native R
comparisons of IDs are exact; `data.table` joins between independent stores
compare 63-bit ID fingerprints. Materialize ID keys when exact cross-store
joining or lexical ordering is required. See `?rad_pack_reads` for details.

## Save data and provenance

Use `rad_save()` and `rad_load()` across R sessions. They serialize a versioned,
materialized payload and recreate native storage on load. Plain `saveRDS()` of
a packed table cannot preserve its native pointers.

```{r save}
saved <- file.path(work, "reads.rds")
rad_save(selected, saved)
restored <- rad_load(saved)
stopifnot(identical(as.character(restored$seq), as.character(selected$seq)))
```

Native workflow results contain the effective configuration and a `core`
provenance record. Preserve these with the analysis outputs. `rad_core_info()`
also reports the embedded RAD version, upstream commit, patched-source digest,
resource digest, and build capabilities:

```{r provenance}
info <- rad_core_info()
info[c("core_version", "source_commit", "embedded_source_digest",
       "resource_digest")]
info$build$openmp
```

Linux can use OpenMP when the configured compiler supports it. The default
macOS installation is serial. Requests for multiple threads on serial builds
warn and use one thread; results report both requested and effective counts.

Small reference layouts and whitelists ship with the package. Large 10x
whitelists are fetched only when requested, from immutable URLs and with byte
count and SHA-256 verification. Before an offline run that needs them, call
`rad_download_whitelists()` while online, then set `options(rrad.offline = TRUE)`.
The `rrad.cache_dir` option or `RRAD_CACHE_DIR` environment variable selects the
cache location. `rad_clear_resource_cache(confirm = TRUE)` removes cached
resources. This vignette enables offline mode throughout and needs no downloads.

```{r cleanup, include=FALSE}
unlink(work, recursive = TRUE)
options(old_options)
```
